clue.text: Information "on painting;, one product of a culture

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it, so the information comes after the painting

parts.note: painting is a form of art
the Roman numeral for one is I
a fact is a piece of information

explanation.surface: Notes about a painting describe a single object made by a civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the information follows the painting and the one. The museum-label surface hides that 'Information', 'painting' and 'one' are three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a made object, such as a tool or pot, that archaeologists study as evidence of a society.

clue.text: Aim for a high position in the church

parts.note: a spire is the tall pointed tower rising from a church roof

explanation.surface: An ambitious cleric hopes for a senior post in the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high position in the church' reads as a bishopric but is taken literally: the spire is physically the highest point of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim at something is to set one's ambition on it, which is what striving upward means.

clue.text: Part in Henry IV for a page taken out

explanation.surface: An actor lands a role in Shakespeare, or a page is ripped from a script.
explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is a tavern prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2. A tear sheet is also a page torn out of a publication, as an advertiser's proof.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is Doll, a Shakespearean character; the other is a perforated page removed from a magazine as a proof.

clue.text: Penalty imposed as result of effort I bungled

indicators.note: something bungled is botched or messed up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A punishment followed because someone's attempt went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' rearranges the seven letters of EFFORT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is something surrendered as a punishment for a fault, as in party games.

clue.text: Do a heart transplant for Tom

annotationWithheld.why: Do a heart transplant for Tom (5) gives CHEAT as C(HE)AT, Tom being CAT, but no clue word supplies HE: only 'Tom' (male) could, doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Do a heart transplant for Tom

clue.text: Figures egghead put out showing relative position

indicators.note: put out means ejected, so a letter is removed from the figures

parts.note: statues are sculpted figures
the head, or first letter, of the word egg is E

explanation.surface: Numbers released by an intellectual reveal where someone ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is split: the head of 'egg' is E, which 'put out' removes from STATUES. 'Figures' wants to be statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank compared with others in a group.

clue.text: A couple on the stage dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the couple comes first

parts.note: a couple is two
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A pair of performers dance together in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stage' suggests a theatre but means a step, as in a stage of a process.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in march or polka time with sliding steps.

clue.text: Garment put over head before one gets cold?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something over turns it upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
the Roman numeral for one is I
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone slips a garment on before feeling the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over head' sounds like dressing, but 'put over' reverses NUT, slang for head, to TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose, sleeveless or short-sleeved garment reaching the hips or knees.

clue.text: Special link person missing on broadcast

indicators.note: special here means specially arranged, so the letters are put into a new order
missing means lacking, so two letters are taken out of the word person

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert presenter is absent from a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing on' takes ON out of PERSON, leaving PERS; 'Special' rearranges PERS with LINK. 'broadcast' looks like radio but is the verb to scatter, as of seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely by hand, as one would spread drops or grains.

clue.text: Clean up state and exact retribution

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for South Carolina, a US state
to avenge is to exact retribution for a wrong

explanation.surface: Tidy the country and take revenge on its enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: Scavenge in an older sense means to clean streets, which is where 'scavenger' as street-cleaner comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Scavenging originally meant removing dirt and refuse from the streets, a municipal cleaning job.

clue.text: Plain glass, used for American vehicle

parts.note: a prairie is a wide grassy plain of North America
a schooner is a tall beer or sherry glass

explanation.surface: Clear glass was used to make something for an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain glass' reads as clear glazing but is two nouns, a grassland and a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The covered wagon of the westward settlers, its white canvas looking like a sail across the grassland, earned this nickname.

clue.text: Characteristic admiration

explanation.walkthrough: A respect is a particular point or feature, as in 'in every respect'; respect is also esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a point or detail, a feature; the other is high regard or esteem.

clue.text: Tax one is able to collect in palace

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a UK sales tax
the Roman numeral for one is I
can means is able

explanation.surface: Tax that a government can gather inside a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax added at each stage of supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the papal palace in Rome, the residence of the Pope.

clue.text: Military HQ. where sides' meetings were obtusely planned

definitions.text: where sides' meetings were obtusely planned

explanation.surface: Generals and opposing sides met at headquarters where talks were planned clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a five-sided figure's sides meet at angles, and in the regular shape every angle is obtuse (108 degrees). 'obtusely' wants to mean stupidly.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Defense Department is housed in a five-sided building in Virginia; a five-sided figure has obtuse interior angles.

clue.text: My most noble quality?

parts.note: the first word turns the phrase into a mild exclamation of surprise, while the rest describes the highest moral virtue

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of the best side of their character.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as boasting, but 'My' plus the answer is a common exclamation of surprise, and the answer is also a virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral excellence is the noblest quality, and the word also completes the cry 'My ...!'.

clue.text: China imprisons father of religious leader

indicators.note: imprisoning shuts one thing inside another, so the father goes inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: The Chinese state jails the father of a faith's head.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, hence PAL. The capital C sells the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal means belonging to the Pope, head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Person in opposition creating hassle about corruption

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for hassle goes around the word for corruption

parts.note: to pester is to hassle or nag
rot means decay or corruption

explanation.surface: An opponent kicks up a fuss over bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'creating' is only a link, though it tempts you to look for an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester objects publicly to something, standing against it.

clue.text: Flier in jet going over the top

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
to cap is to cover the top of something, or go one better

explanation.surface: A passenger on an aircraft goes beyond the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier in jet' paints an air passenger; the flier is a bird and jet is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackcap is a warbler, a small songbird; the male has a black crown.

clue.text: Relaxation allowed at university

parts.note: let means allowed
up means in residence at university, as at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Students are given time off while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' at university while in residence and 'goes down' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off in effort or intensity.

clue.text: In examination, learner gets mark for difficult question

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the learner sits within the examination

parts.note: a probe is a searching examination
L is for learner, as on the L-plates of a British learner driver
M is short for mark, as in Mark 2 or a German mark

explanation.surface: A student taking a test earns a score on a tricky item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In examination' puts L inside PROBE; M follows. The exam-room surface hides that 'mark' is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a hard question set to be solved, as in mathematics.

clue.text: Obvious person to start taking bets

explanation.surface: A transparent character is about to begin accepting wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: An open book is a person easy to read; a bookmaker who opens a book begins accepting bets on an event.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is someone whose thoughts are plain to see; the other is a bookmaker beginning to accept wagers.

clue.text: Transferred thug into communications business

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the thug goes within the company initials

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, is the UK telephone company
a rough is a violent hooligan

explanation.surface: A gangster was moved into a telephone company.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom, Britain's main telephone company.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought means carried or conveyed somewhere, moved from one place to another.

clue.text: Attempt to hold object in

indicators.note: hold means contain, so the attempt grips the object inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Try to keep the item inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the definition, meaning fashionable; it looks like part of a phrase 'hold ... in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is fashionable or in vogue, the current style.

clue.text: Had a close shave, being felled

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly escaped as a tree came down.
explanation.walkthrough: A beard cut down is trimmed short; a tree or soldier cut down is felled. 'close shave' suggests a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is trimmed short, as hair or growth is reduced; the other is chopped to the ground, as a tree is.

clue.text: A writer or two

explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain was the American author of Tom Sawyer; twain is an old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the pen-name of the novelist Samuel Clemens; the other is an archaic word for a pair.

clue.text: Individual in party installing extra road, initially

definitions.text: Individual in party installing extra road, initially

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the individual sits within the initial letters
initially means taking the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: One member of a working party lays an additional road.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE goes inside PIER, the first letters of 'party installing extra road'. A pioneer was a soldier who went ahead building roads, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Military pioneers were advance troops sent ahead to make roads and clear the way for the army.

clue.text: Hotel in a foreign place

explanation.surface: A guest stays in a hotel in a square abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plaza is a famous New York hotel; a plaza is a public square in a Spanish town.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the grand New York hotel; the other is the Spanish word for a town square.

clue.text: Old actor finding something amusing in dance

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the amusing thing goes within the dance

parts.note: the Charleston is a lively 1920s dance
a laugh is something funny, as in 'what a laugh'

explanation.surface: A veteran performer enjoys a joke during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Laughton was a British-born film star of the 1930s, famous as Henry VIII and Quasimodo.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the British-born film star of the 1930s, famous as Henry VIII and Quasimodo.

clue.text: Protection for head of state

explanation.surface: A national leader is given security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like one phrase, but splits into a hat and a country.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the straw hat worn against the sun; the other is the Central American country.

clue.text: Expert alters my composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A skilled writer changes the music I wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ALTERS and MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterly means showing great skill, like the work of an accomplished craftsman.
